QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_30

question.text: Himadri Growth Fund's unliquidated portfolio is valued at INR 120 crore. The Manager arranges bids totalling INR 24 crore for in-specie distribution purposes. At what value will the unliquidated investments be distributed in-specie?

answer.text: INR 24 crore (bid value, because bids are ≥ 25% threshold).
INR 120 crore (full NAV, because bids are arranged).
ONE RUPEE (because INR 24 crore bids are below the 25% of INR 120 crore = INR 30 crore threshold).

explanation.text: The Logic: 25% of INR 120 crore = INR 30 crore. The bids arranged (INR 24 crore) are BELOW this 25% threshold. Per Chapter 12: 'One Rupee, if the AIF or its Manager fails to arrange bids for a minimum of 25% of the value of unliquidated investments of the Original Scheme.' Distribution happens at ONE RUPEE for performance-benchmarking purposes. If bids had been INR 30 crore or more, in-specie would occur at bid value. The Trap: Distributing at the shortfall bid value (Option A) ignores the threshold rule. Full NAV (Option B) is never the fallback. INR 30 crore (Option C) is an invented 'floor' — the actual rule is binary: bid value (if ≥25%) OR One Rupee. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same binary. XIX-B (Cat III distributor) does not cover this mechanism. XIX-D expects precise numerical application. Manager's Pro-Tip: The 'One Rupee' outcome is a career-defining blow to a Manager's performance track record. Start bid-solicitation 18+ months before liquidation-period expiry, target multiple bidders, and price at realistic (not anchor) valuations.
